title: Two unvaccinated people die from measles in Pennsylvania, officials confirm
summary: Two unvaccinated individuals in Pennsylvania have died from measles, marking the first measles deaths in the state in 35 years and part of a rising trend in the US. Measles cases are surging due to declining vaccination rates, which have fallen below the 95% threshold needed for herd immunity. The CDC reports 2,777 cases in 2026, the highest since 1991. The MMR vaccine is highly effective and safe, but misinformation and anti-vaccine rhetoric have contributed to reduced vaccination rates.
key_points: Two unvaccinated individuals in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, died from measles, the first such deaths in the state in 35 years.
The US has reported 2,777 measles cases in 2026, the highest since 1991, due to declining vaccination rates.
Vaccination rates in the US have dropped to around 92%, below the 95% threshold required for herd immunity.
Non-medical vaccination exemptions have reached a record high of 4% in 2026.
In Pennsylvania, measles vaccination rates fell from 96.7% in 2017 to 92.7% in 2026, with Lancaster County reporting only 87.6% vaccination among kindergartners.

Measles can lead to severe complications, including hospitalizations, hearing loss, intellectual disabilities, and a rare fatal neurological condition called subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE).
Two doses of the MMR vaccine are 97% effective against measles and have been proven safe through rigorous testing and decades of use.
Misinformation and anti-vaccine rhetoric, including false claims by public figures, have contributed to reduced confidence in vaccines.
